newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists still behind, gaining slowly--poll.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists still behind, gaining slowly--poll.

text.p: The French Socialists are slowly gaining ground ahead of a May 25-June 1 parliamentary election but the ruling centre-right retains a comfortable lead, according to an opinion poll published on Wednesday.
The Louis Harris poll for the magazine Valeurs Actuelles saw the centre-right coalition retaining power with a reduced majority of 302 seats to 251 for the left and ecologists.
A CSA poll released on Tuesday had put the centre-right majority at a narrower 296 to 258.
The Louis Harris survey saw the ruling RPR-UDF coalition polling 39 percent of the votes, unchanged from the previous week.
It saw the Socialists polling 28 percent, up from 26 percent a week ago, while their Communist allies polled 10 percent and the ecologists 6.5 percent, each down 0.5 percent.
The far-right National Front was down 1.5 percent at 14.5 percent, projected to win two seats.
Thirty percent of the 1,003 people questioned said they could still change their minds.
President Jacques Chirac's standing rose slightly to 37 percent from 35 the previous week, with the percentage of those dissatisfied with him slipping to 58 from 60 percent.

The standing of Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who is leading the conservatives' campaign, slipped one percentage point to 30 percent while the percentage of those dissatisfied was unchanged at 65 percent.
